_doc: The numbers and names prep.py runs on: how it batches, retries and times out the Source2Viewer-CLI (VRF) exports from the player's CS2 VPK, and where it looks for weapon stats items_game.txt does not give. Read from prep/prep.json (a copy of this sheet) on the player's PC. The rows are this build's choices; vdata_keys maps CS2 weapon vdata fields to the items_game attribute names Weapons.gd reads, every one unverified until a real CS2 weapons.vdata has been read.

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.export: most VPK paths in one VRF -f call
rows.note: fewer calls means less VRF start-up time (it opens the 30+ GB VPK index each run)

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.export: longest comma-joined -f list in one VRF call
rows.note: Windows CreateProcess caps a command line at 32767 characters; this keeps a call far under it with long install paths
rows.verified: build choice; the 32767 limit is the documented Windows CreateProcess limit

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.export: after the batched calls, each file that still failed the output check is exported again on its own this many times
rows.note: one file per call on a retry, so one bad path cannot cost the rest of its batch
rows.verified: build choice; tested with a fake VRF that drops files (prep/tests/test_export.py)

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.run_vrf: a VRF call that runs longer is killed and its files count as failed (then retried)
rows.note: the 0.1.0 install exported 5 models and clips in one call well inside this; 40 weapon models per call is unmeasured
rows.verified: build choice, unverified against a real 40-model call

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.cs2_step: exported on its own after items_game.txt; read by prep/kv3.py for any stat items_game.txt does not give, and compared with items_game.txt where both give one (stats_conflict_winner)
rows.note: optional: a VPK without it is not a problem by itself, only weapons left without the stats in stats_required are
rows.verified: unverified: path from memory of CS2 modding notes, not seen in a VPK listing here

rows.value: damage,cycletime,primary clip size,is full auto,armor ratio,penetration,range modifier,spread,inaccuracy stand,inaccuracy crouch,inaccuracy move,inaccuracy fire,recoil angle,recoil angle variance,recoil magnitude,recoil magnitude variance,recoil seed,recovery time stand,recovery time crouch,max player speed
rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: every weapons.json gun (slot not in stats_light_slots) is checked for every one of these as a number, from items_game.txt or weapons.vdata; a gap is a player-visible warning naming the weapon and the keys, or a problem that stops setup when stats_required_blocks is yes. Weapons.gd reads the same list and names any gun missing one in the error panel
rows.note: every stat Weapons.gd reads for damage, armor, penetration, falloff, fire mode, spread, inaccuracy, recoil pattern and recovery: a CS2 update that moves one of them is named on screen instead of the gun quietly running on weapon_defaults.json class averages
rows.verified: build choice; tested in prep/tests/test_prep.py (a missing or non-numeric attribute is named as a warning, and blocks the done file when stats_required_blocks is yes). Which keys the real CS2 items_game.txt/weapons.vdata carry per gun is unverified here: CS:GO's items_game.txt gave all of them per weapon prefab chain

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: yes makes a stats_required (or stats_required_light) gap a problem (no done file, setup reruns on every start); no makes it a warning in prep_status.json that the game shows
rows.note: no until a real CS2 install has been read: the key names are unverified, and a wrong one would otherwise fail setup on every start for every player. Setup still stops when items_game.txt does not export or parse, or names no entry for a weapon
rows.verified: build choice (gauntlet round 3 critics: an unverified key name must not brick every install); tested in prep/tests/test_prep.py both ways

rows.used_by: prep.py finish: on Windows a failed setup also opens a message box with the reasons; prep exits when it is closed or after this long
rows.note: the reasons stay in data/prep.log and the game's error panel either way; the box is for the case where the launcher's console window closes before the player can read it. --no-dialog or RS_PREP_NO_DIALOG=1 turns it off
rows.verified: build choice; whether Melty shows setup's console output is unverified (MODLOG), and the box itself is only exercised with a stub in prep/tests (no Windows here)

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: guns in these slots need only stats_required_light
rows.note: the Zeus x27 fires one charge with no recoil pattern, so its recoil and inaccuracy keys are not required

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: the required stats for stats_light_slots guns
rows.note: damage, rate, charge count and the Zeus's short reach; everything else of the Zeus comes from the gear row of weapon_defaults.json
rows.verified: build choice; whether CS2's taser entry carries 'range' is unverified (CS:GO's did)

rows.value: headshot multiplier,primary reserve ammo max,range,inaccuracy jump initial,inaccuracy land
rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: a gun missing any of these still finishes setup, with a warning in prep_status.json naming the weapon and the keys (those values come from weapon_defaults.json class columns)
rows.note: keys with one engine-wide value in CS:GO (headshot x4) or that only shape secondary feel; zoom and alt keys are left out because only some guns have them
rows.verified: build choice; the CS:GO key names are from its items_game.txt, the CS2 file is unverified here

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: when both files give a number for the same stat of a gun and they differ (by more than stats_conflict_tolerance), this file's value goes into weapon_stats.json (which Weapons.gd reads over the raw items_game.txt); every such pair is logged in prep.log and kept under the gun's _conflicts. tools/package.py refuses a release with any conflict while this row's verified cell still says unverified
rows.note: items_game.txt was CS:GO's stats file; CS2 also ships weapons.vdata, and a value tuned only there would lose to a stale items_game.txt attribute. A disagreement can equally be a wrong vdata_keys mapping, so the packager settles it on the packaging PC's real files and marks this row verified
rows.verified: unverified: which of the two files CS2 itself plays from was not checked here (no CS2 install); tested both ways in prep/tests/test_prep.py and the release refusal in prep/tests/test_release.py

rows.used_by: prep_cs2.write_stats: two numbers closer than this are the same value (0.1 written as 0.100000 or 0.1 is no conflict)
rows.note: the same tolerance Weapons.gd --wtest stats_reference compares known values with
